intended_object: The subgroup Div⁰_w(X) of divisors (finitely supported formal ℤ-combinations of points) whose weighted degree ∑ n_x·w(x) is zero. For a curve over k with w(x) = [κ(x):k], this is the usual group of degree-zero divisors. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
In this library `WeilDivisor X` is `X →₀ ℤ`, the free abelian group on the points of X. `weightedDegree w` is the additive homomorphism `D ↦ ∑ D(x)·w(x)`, built from `Finsupp.linearCombination ℤ w`. The definition takes its kernel, so it is exactly the subgroup of divisors of weighted degree zero.

It is stated for an arbitrary type of points and an arbitrary integer weight. That is the most general setting the construction makes sense in, so it is not too narrow. With w(x) = [κ(x):k] on a curve over k, it gives the usual degree-zero divisor group, as the docstring says. I found no Mathlib definition of degree-zero Weil divisors; the general pieces it relies on (`Finsupp.linearCombination`, `AddMonoidHom.ker`) are already Mathlib's.
